### 1. Determination of $Dq$ and $B$
The complex $[Co(H_2O)_6]^{2+}$ is a high-spin $d^7$ octahedral system. The ground state is $^4T_{1g}(F)$. The observed quartet-quartet transitions are:
- $\nu_1 = 8,100 \text{ cm}^{-1}$ (assigned to $^4T_{1g}(F) \to ^4T_{2g}$)
- $\nu_2 = 19,400 \text{ cm}^{-1}$ (assigned to $^4T_{1g}(F) \to ^4T_{1g}(P)$)

For $d^7$ high-spin octahedral complexes, the ratio $\nu_2 / \nu_1$ is used to find the $Dq/B$ ratio from a Tanabe-Sugano diagram:
$$\frac{\nu_2}{\nu_1} = \frac{19,400}{8,100} \approx 2.395$$
From the Tanabe-Sugano diagram for $d^7$, a ratio of $\approx 2.40$ corresponds to $Dq/B \approx 0.96$.
At $Dq/B = 0.96$, the ratio $\nu_1/B$ is approximately $8.6$. We can now calculate $B$:
$$B = \frac{\nu_1}{8.6} = \frac{8,100 \text{ cm}^{-1}}{8.6} \approx 942 \text{ cm}^{-1}$$
Using $Dq/B = 0.96$:
$$Dq = 0.96 \times 942 \text{ cm}^{-1} \approx 904 \text{ cm}^{-1}$$
Checking $\nu_2$: $\nu_2/B \approx 20.6$ at this $Dq/B$.
$$\nu_2 = 20.6 \times 942 \approx 19,405 \text{ cm}^{-1}$$

$$21,600 = 15(942) + 3C - 4(904)$$
$$21,600 = 14,130 + 3C - 3,616$$
$$21,600 = 10,514 + 3C$$
$$3C = 11,086 \implies C \approx 3,695 \text{ cm}^{-1}$$
Calculating the ratio $C/B$:
$$C/B = 3,695 / 942 \approx 3.92$$
This is consistent with the typical value for transition metals where $C \approx 4B$.
